Site search Slow Pacman downloads on Arch Linux? Follow our guide to optimize and speed up your package manager for a smoother experience. If you are experiencing slow downloads with Pacman on Arch Linux, you are not alone. Sometimes system updates through pacman, or package installations in general, slow down on an Arch system. This can be frustrating, especially when downloading large packages.

When download speeds drop, first distinguish between local network performance, an individual mirror, and all mirrors.
There are several ways to address the issue. Let’s go through them.
But why are downloads slow? There can be several reasons, some of which may relate to your system configuration:
Internet speed or network connectivity problems
Mirror server load or connectivity problems
Out-of-date Arch Linux mirrors
How to fix slow downloads with Pacman on Arch Linux
Now that we have discussed the causes of slow downloads, let’s move on to the solutions. Here are several step-by-step approaches to fixing slow Pacman downloads on Arch Linux:
Use a different Pacman server

One of the simplest ways to fix slow downloads on Arch Linux is to use a different Pacman server. You can try a Pacman mirror closer to your country or region, or choose a less busy mirror to improve download speeds. Enable parallel downloads

By default, Pacman downloads packages sequentially, which can reduce download speed. You can enable parallel downloads to download several packages at once and improve throughput.

Clean your Pacman cache

The cache primarily affects disk usage and does not generally slow down network downloads. If the disk is full or I/O is a bottleneck, investigate storage rather than treating cache cleanup as a universal download-speed fix. Keeping older packages also helps with troubleshooting and reinstallation.

pacman -Sc cleans cached packages and unused repository databases according to its policy and prompts. A more controlled option is paccache -r, which keeps the three most recent versions of each package by default.
Use a download manager

A download manager can split a download into several parts to make it faster and more efficient. You can use a command-line download manager such as wget or uget for a faster download experience. Finally, another option is to check your internet connection and switch to a faster one if needed. If your ISP plan provides a low-bandwidth Wi-Fi or wired connection, you may need a higher-bandwidth plan.
Slow downloads can be frustrating, but they are a common problem that can be straightforward to solve. The methods above can significantly improve Pacman download speeds on Arch Linux.
